nodes.label: SOAP/WSDL Integration Surface
nodes.rationale: Scryba Sign exposes signing, timestamping, authentication, document retrieval, and validation capabilities through versioned SOAP Web Services described by WSDL contracts.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: HTTPS with Basic Authentication
nodes.rationale: Basic Authentication credentials are only encoded, so HTTPS is required to protect Web Service communication.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: CAdES, PAdES, XAdES, and Hash Signing
nodes.author: Medas
nodes.norm_label: cades, pades, xades, and hash signing

nodes.label: Simplified Remote Signature
nodes.rationale: The simplified procedure omits OTP only when the authenticated and authorised Signer App enforces session timeout and appropriate user authentication controls.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: Signing Power and Signature Profile
nodes.rationale: A configured certificate alone does not authorise signing; a signer must also have a signing power that binds eligible certificates to a signature profile and its permitted document origins and types.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: FDR, Smart Card, and FEA Certificate Types
nodes.author: Medas
nodes.norm_label: fdr, smart card, and fea certificate types

nodes.label: Synchronous Signing Workflow
nodes.rationale: The Signer App controls credential collection and either signs one document in one call or manages a stateful session for a batch of documents.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: Asynchronous Signing Workflow
nodes.rationale: The Signer App enqueues documents, directs the user to the Scryba Sign signing page, polls for completion, retrieves the signed document, and acknowledges acquisition by requesting deletion.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: Graphometric Signature Workflow
nodes.rationale: The graphometric workflow resembles the asynchronous scenario but accepts one document per session and carries the ordered graphical-signature information required by the signing device.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: OpenSignSession, SignDoc, CloseSignSession Chain
nodes.rationale: The returned session identifier is propagated to subsequent calls so multiple documents use the same certificate and one credential acquisition.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: OpenSignSession, EnqueueDoc, CloseSignSession Chain
nodes.rationale: The asynchronous batch chain opens an upload session, obtains a document UID for each enqueue operation, and closes the session with an action that commits or cancels signing.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: getDocumentStatus GET/DELETE Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: The client polls with GET until the signed document is available and then uses DELETE to acknowledge acquisition and end server-side availability.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: GetUserInfo4
nodes.rationale: The method returns the signer's powers, certificates, and OTP devices so the Signer App can construct a valid signing request and user interface.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: digitalStamp V1.0 WSDL
nodes.rationale: Digital stamping produces a verifiable PDF copy; flattening preserves the visual signature objects but does not preserve pre-existing digital signatures as cryptographic layers.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: Large-file SFTP and SHA-256 Transfer Procedure
nodes.rationale: For documents larger than 10 MB, the binary is transferred outside the SOAP envelope through certificate-authenticated SFTP and correlated to the signing request by its SHA-256 digest.
nodes.author: Medas
nodes.norm_label: large-file sftp and sha-256 transfer procedure

nodes.label: SPID/CIE-based Automatic FEA Enrolment
nodes.rationale: A trusted SPID or CIE identification flow can support automatic FEA certificate issuance while preserving explicit user consent and document-preview requirements.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: Medas Device Manager
nodes.rationale: Physical devices such as smart cards, graphometric tablets, and scanners are mediated by the Device Manager client rather than accessed directly through the server integration surface.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: Synthetic Test Documents and Metadata
nodes.rationale: Integration testing must not use documents or metadata that identify real persons.
nodes.author: Medas

nodes.label: Integration Certification Process
nodes.rationale: The integration is first exercised independently in a test environment and then verified through a joint test with temporary certificates or test access.
nodes.author: Medas
